summary: IDS feed s181_triple is degraded: 28.5% one-way TCP sessions, 11% jumbo frames exceeding IDS MTU, and 3.42 Gbps microbursts overloading 1 Gbps port causing detection blind spots.

findings.root_cause: 35 of 123 TCP sessions (28.5%) show only one direction, exceeding 10% threshold. Most likely SPAN/mirror configured for single direction, asymmetric routing with single-sided TAP, or packet broker hash splitting client/server directions to different tool ports without bidirectional aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly and stateful detection. One-way traffic prevents stream reassembly, flow tracking, and signature matching - IDS will miss exploits, C2, and produce false negatives on 28% of sessions.

params.mode: aggregate both directions to same IDS port/group

recommended_fix.why: IDS is stateful and needs client+server packets on same port to reassemble. Aggregate both directions via packet broker flow-aware hashing or TAP aggregation to deliver complete sessions.

findings.root_cause: 185 of 1675 frames (11.0%) exceed IDS port MTU of 1518 bytes, largest 8058 bytes. Network is forwarding jumbo frames (likely 9000 MTU DC/storage traffic) while IDS 1G NIC is standard Ethernet MTU and drops oversize frames at ingress.
findings.impact_on_tool: NIC drops 11% of frames before IDS inspection. IDS has complete blind spot for jumbo payloads and cannot detect exploits in large frames. Tool needs full payload so slicing/trimming is not an option.

recommended_fix.why: Cannot use slicing because IDS needs_full_payload=true. Must enable jumbo support (9000 MTU) on IDS NIC/tool or normalize MTU upstream, or filter/forward jumbos to a jumbo-capable IDS instance.

findings.root_cause: Peak 3.42 Gbps in 1ms burst vs 1 Gbps IDS port (342% of capacity, 6 overloaded intervals). Sustained microbursts exceed tool port speed due to no load balancing or rate limiting on packet broker egress.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port buffers overflow and drops packets during bursts. Results in missed detection, broken TCP reassembly, and gaps in IDS coverage precisely during high-traffic attack windows.

params.strategy: horizontal load balance or upgrade port

recommended_fix.why: Distribute 3.42 Gbps bursts across multiple 1 Gbps IDS ports via packet broker load-balancing (flow-aware) or upgrade to 10 Gbps tool port to eliminate drops and preserve full payload to IDS.
